past_actions.summary: Schedule a meeting with branch manager to formally flag the sustained 50% application volume decline and request a portfolio diversification conversation — specifically, cross-training or reassignment to support mortgage or small business lending.
past_actions.emotional_state: Controlled concern. Not panicking — panic is expensive — but the low-grade alarm is there. I sleep fine but I'm thinking about this more than I'd like. The feeling isn't dread, it's more like the feeling you get when you realize the weather is changing and you're still deciding whether to grab a jacket. You're not wet yet. You're not going to be wet if you move now.

past_actions.summary: Block 90 minutes daily on calendar for mortgage underwriting and SBA 7(a)/504 loan training. Contact the regional training coordinator to formally enroll in the next available NMLS-approved mortgage origination course. Request access to the bank's internal SBA loan files from the past two years to self-study deal structures. Set a 30-day milestone: complete modules 1-4 of mortgage origination curriculum and shadow at least two live mortgage closings.
past_actions.emotional_state: Grounded. The confirmation of what I already suspected is not frightening — it is clarifying. I feel the kind of calm that comes from having moved first. There is a small undertow of pressure knowing that the institutional gears are now turning above me and timelines may compress, but that pressure is productive. I am not in denial, I am not catastrophizing. I am a 44-year-old professional who has done this work for two decades and still has runway, savings, a supportive manager, and a bank that needs people who can do more than one thing. The next 60 days matter. I will make them count.

past_actions.summary: Apply today for Maria Santos's $2,500 retraining grant through the council program. The NMLS mortgage origination course costs approximately $300-600 depending on employer reimbursement status. The grant covers this and potentially additional SBA certification costs. Complete the application form, attach proof of enrollment in the NMLS-approved course, and submit before end of business. This is a no-downside action — the grant is available, Kevin is eligible, the application takes two hours, and it offsets real out-of-pocket training costs.
past_actions.emotional_state: Focused and slightly accelerated. The calm from tick 1 is still the foundation, but the word-of-mouth about David's memo introduces a new variable: institutional timelines are now outside my direct control in a way they were not before. That is not alarming — it is information. The right response is compression, not panic. I am moving the closing shadow up, filing the grant today, and making sure David sees my progress before Sandra does. This is still methodical. It is methodical with a tighter clock.

past_actions.summary: Formally accept David Chen's structured NMLS mortgage licensing pathway. Send written acknowledgment to David confirming: acceptance of the 8-month timeline, intent to use tuition reimbursement for the NMLS-approved course, readiness to begin co-originator exposure on live mortgage files as soon as David can schedule it. Request a formal first check-in at the 30-day mark. This locks in the institutional commitment from both sides and signals to David — and anyone watching — that Kevin is a reliable investment, not a flight risk.

Prepare a written one-page brief for David Chen's formal 30-minute check-in: document the early delinquency patterns I have observed firsthand on auto loans processed in the last 60 days, note the 18% application volume decline I am seeing on the front end, and confirm NMLS module completion progress (modules 1-3 complete, modules 4-6 on schedule). Bring this brief to the meeting as a tangible deliverable — not a presentation, just one page showing I have been paying attention to the same data David is sharing upward. Ask David directly what the new written underwriting criteria will look like and request a draft copy so I can align my intake workflow before it is formally published.

reflections.reflection: Six ticks in and I am still employed, still in the retraining pipeline, still burning savings at a rate that is manageable but not comfortable. The word-of-mouth about David is the most destabilizing signal I have received so far — not because I know what it means, but because I don't. Every structural move I have made since tick 0 has been anchored to David Chen's sponsorship of my NMLS pathway. If that sponsorship walks out the door with him, I have a tuition reimbursement form and a training log that lives only on my personal calendar. That is not enough. I should have filed the HR paperwork two ticks ago. I did not. I kept treating the verbal agreement as sufficient because David had been reliable and I did not want to look like I was hedging against him. That was a mistake.
reflections.identity_shift: I am beginning to separate my professional identity from the bank as an institution and reattach it to the skills I am building. For the first decade of my career I was 'a loan officer at First Community Bank.' Now I am increasingly thinking of myself as someone who understands credit, risk, and financial access — and who happens to currently work at a bank. That shift is subtle but it matters. It means the NMLS license is not just a hedge against one role disappearing. It is the foundation of something portable.
regrets: Did not file the NMLS co-originator paperwork with HR in ticks 4 or 5 — left the institutional commitment floating on David's personal goodwill rather than making it structural.

Waited too long to make myself visible to community stakeholders like Lisa Freeman. There was an obvious opportunity to be the human face of bank lending products for the retraining pipeline and I did not move on it until now.
successes: Delivered the tick 5 brief to David — concrete, data-grounded, showed I was watching the same metrics he was reporting upward. That was the right move regardless of what happens to David's role.
NMLS modules 1-3 complete and on schedule. The 90-minute daily block has held for five ticks. That is real.

Identified and acted on the Lisa Freeman outreach opportunity this tick before it became irrelevant. Positioning myself as the operational link between bank products and retraining enrollees creates value that any manager would recognize.
reflections.adaptation_notes: Primary risk this tick: manager-level instability threatening the institutional NMLS pathway. Mitigation: formalize through HR immediately, make the paperwork independent of any single person. Secondary opportunity: the community retraining pipeline needs someone with financial product knowledge who can sit in a room and answer questions. I am that person. Monthly office hours at the Community Center is low-cost, high-visibility, and directly responsive to what Lisa Freeman has been trying to build. If David is gone and I need a new manager to see my value, being the banker who shows up at the Community Center is the kind of story that travels. Financial note: at current burn rate I have approximately 6-7 months of runway. The training pathway must produce a concrete role change before month 8 or the math stops working.
